summary.headline: eClerx Q1FY27 operating revenue rose 15.2% YoY to USD 125.9M with 2.8% QoQ growth, its 12th straight sequential increase; EBITDA margin 23%.
summary.overview: Q1FY27 operating revenue was USD 125.9M (up 15.2% YoY, 2.8% QoQ) and INR 11,524M (up 23% YoY), the 12th consecutive quarter of sequential growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 2,652M at 23% margin, down 260 bps QoQ mainly on wage increments, and PAT was INR 1,643M (14% margin). New deal wins were USD 41M (up 25% YoY). BFSI was roughly flat QoQ and Media/Retail/Fashion remained soft, while Analytics and Automation crossed a USD 100M annual run rate. Management reiterated a 24-28% full-year EBITDA margin range and top-quartile growth for FY27, and said it expects another sequential increase in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: -260 bps QoQ (wages 210 bps, computers/network 40 bps, S&D offset -60 bps); -96 bps YoY
Lower on reduced investable surplus; total revenue INR 11,702M, +24% YoY
OCF/EBITDA 38%, seasonally low due to FY26 variable pay payout in Q1
Billed headcount up on higher utilization

segments.name: Analytics and Automation / Technology & Analytics
segments.commentary: Grew 7% QoQ, ahead of company average, and crossed a USD 100M annual run rate. Management cites AI demand in Hi-tech and BFSI, with data preparation and exploratory data analysis as early entry points.

segments.name: BFSI (Financial Services)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 0.1% QoQ after -2.8% in Q4 and -3% to -3.5% in the prior quarter. Management expects growth from H2FY27; early wins include a Fayetteville contact-centre deal and mortgage servicing work in the US.

segments.name: CMT (Communication, Media & Telecom)
segments.commentary: QoQ growth slowed to 1.3% from 7% in Q4, which management called a quarterly aberration unrelated to US regulation. International centres Cairo, Manila and Fayetteville grew.

segments.name: Hi-tech and M&D / Retail
segments.commentary: Hi-tech outlook described as positive; Hi-tech and M&D saw a growth turnaround. Retail and M&D described as soft due to Middle East-related supply chain pressure. Fashion & Luxury flat QoQ and +2% YoY.

segments.name: Emerging business (F&A-led)
segments.commentary: Strong growth for the fourth consecutive quarter; expanding F&A support to APAC for one client and moving from SMB into mid-market.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected within 24-28%; management advised the midpoint (~26%) as more realistic, since FY26 closed at 27%.
Top-quartile revenue growth among listed peers reaffirmed for FY27; management believes Q1 was also top-quartile.
Expects sequential revenue growth in Q2FY27, with quarter-on-quarter variation acknowledged.
Margins expected to improve QoQ from Q2 onward if revenue grows, since Q1 carried the annual increments.
CMT/Fashion & Luxury: full-year CLX growth guided at about 0% to 2%; Q2 seasonally soft.
Capex for FY27 guided at INR 130-150 crore; three-year capex to be set in next year's budget.
FY27 ACV aspiration to exceed the ~USD 170M achieved in FY26.
Investor Day planned later in the quarter.
BFSI growth turn expected from H2FY27.
capex_capacity: Adding about 1,600 seats across Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh, Mohali and Coimbatore, becoming operational in a staggered manner over the next three to four months.
Seat count dipped slightly in Q1 as some production seats were refitted; the new capacity also drives higher Ind AS depreciation and interest.
Coimbatore operations started in Q1, supporting delivery and talent access.
Spend on computers, servers and network infrastructure rose; management expects communication and networking costs not to fall as a share of revenue near term because equipment is more expensive.
Cairo and Lima set up 12-15 months ago; Manila headcount doubled over 15 months. Lower gross-margin locations are growing faster, which dilutes margin.
demand_pricing: Roll-off guided at 15-20% of revenue over a four-quarter period, expected to hold for FY27 though quarterly volatile.
Deal sizes in AI are relatively small; management described AI revenue as icing on the cake, not yet a material share.
Pricing pressure from competitors acknowledged but described as nothing extraordinary; total cost of ownership is the main buying criterion.
Top-5 client softness attributed to a lower refresh cycle in US FCC due to a less onerous regulatory environment, not to client-specific weakness.
Non-top-10 clients are a stated priority to reduce concentration; quarterly volatility noted.
Inbound interest up after analyst recognition; management says deal sizes are increasing.
QA 360 pilot with a large CMT client goes live in Q2, auditing about 0.5M interactions per month.

qa_highlights.question: Is BFSI lagging a concern, and when will it catch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BFSI was flat QoQ and expects momentum and benefits from H2FY27 based on pipeline and conversions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI and technology investment reflected in headcount, and when will it pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Investments include an AI COE, pilots and product enhancements. Tech & Analytics growth of about 7% is cited as the proxy; ROI is judged by growth, conversions and margins within 24-28%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did headcount decline, and is growth at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Total headcount fell but billed headcount rose on higher utilization. Management reiterated sequential growth and top-quartile FY27 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a US regulatory impact on CMT, and what is happening with top-5 clients?
qa_highlights.answer: No regulatory change in either direction. CMT slowdown called a quarterly aberration; top-5 softness linked to lower FCC refresh cycles as US financial regulation has eased.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin changes and FX impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding FX, QoQ margin impact would have been 330 bps, mostly increments. FX contributed about 50 bps QoQ. Management expects margins to rise from here.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and revenue guidance for the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex INR 130-150 crore. Three-year capex will be set in next year's budget. Top-quartile growth guidance unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold as the company grows toward USD 1B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to stay within 24-28% if tech, analytics and AI reach 30-40% of revenue, despite competitive pressure.

risks_watch: Q2FY27 sequential revenue growth is guided, but management acknowledged quarter-on-quarter variation; roll-off is volatile and is guided at 15-20% of revenue over four quarters.
BFSI has been flat to negative for consecutive quarters (-2.8% in Q4, -0.1% in Q1); the H2FY27 turnaround is the key test.

Margin: Q1 carried annual increments and FY27 EBITDA guidance is 24-28%, with management steering to the midpoint (~26%); investment in tech, AI, new centres (Cairo, Manila, Lima) and G&A (communication/networking) is dilutive.
Top-5 client softness attributed to lower US FCC refresh cycles under lighter regulation; CMT slowed to 1.3% QoQ, called an aberration, needs confirmation in Q2.
ACV trajectory: management aspires to exceed ~USD 170M in FY27, but the call acknowledged quarterly variability and that AI deal sizes are still small.
Capex of INR 130-150 crore for FY27 and ~1,600 seats coming online over three to four months; watch for depreciation and interest drag and three-year capex to be set in next year's budget.
Investor Day planned later this quarter, where details on the $1B ambition and strategy are expected.
key_quotes: Even so, we expect another quarter of sequential growth.

And from a margin standpoint, will it mimic last year's trajectory in terms of quarter -on-quarter margin improvement? Margins will continue to improve because this quarter is when we gave out the increments.
So, I think the midpoint is what you should pick because higher than that is going to be a little bit difficult.
There is no further change in either direction from what we reported in the last quarter.
So, we're already beginning to see the change.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the top-quartile growth, sequential growth in Q2 and the 24-28% margin range, but was noticeably cautious on BFSI, where it gave only directional timing (H2FY27). It was evasive on specifics such as AI revenue share, ACV trend and the mortgage opportunity size, deferring these to later updates or the Investor Day.

adds.what: About 1,600 seats across Mumbai, Pune, Chandigarh, Mohali and Coimbatore

growth.why: Management reiterated top-quartile FY27 revenue growth, expects sequential growth in Q2, and is adding about 1,600 seats becoming operational over 3-4 months, but BFSI is flat and Media/Retail soft, so I score it +1 rather than +2.
